analysis:
Units 83da50da4dbbb821:4 and :5 are BASE text of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift (lines 912-1725). The head-side hunks (new stopsAsked/serveUnlessStopped, followerStatus, localServe(unlessStoppedSince:), stopsBefore) are only partly visible through a truncated patch excerpt (patch_excerpt_complete=false), so the new serve/stop sequencing logic is not fully reviewed.

What the base text shows: the provisioning, adopt, serve, register and setScope flows. The command() helper at ~1496 sends over the paired cluster link, and localServe at ~1681 writes serving=true and then issues a .serve command. The head change threads a stop counter through the status reply and conditions serve on no stop having been requested since. This looks like a race-fix for a stop-vs-serve ordering problem, an availability/consistency issue within the owner's paired two-Mac link rather than a coordinator or consumer boundary.

Security-relevant observations: no change is visible to the model artifact verification path (manifest SHA-256 check, servableArtifacts, approved()), the coordinator registration (ClusterApprovalSync), or the App Attest and authorization trust (TB-011, T-052/T-053). The new fields are unauthenticated-looking additions to ClusterControlReply/Request, but the transport is the paired, authenticated link (ClusterSetupLinkExchange.command with a pairing). I cannot verify here that the stopsBefore value is validated on the receiving side or that the reply is bound to the claim.

Open questions for integration: (1) whether serve(unlessStoppedSince:) fails closed, and does not serve after a person's stop, on a counter reset or a restart; (2) whether stopsAsked persists in the record with owner-only permissions; (3) whether the head's behavior on an older peer, which ignores the fields, can restart a pair the person stopped, which is an availability concern only. No concrete regression is supportable from the supplied evidence.
